newsitem.title: CANADA: Rio Algom Ltd jumps amid takeover rumors.
newsitem.headline: Rio Algom Ltd jumps amid takeover rumors.

text.p: Shares in Rio Algom Ltd jumped on the Toronto Stock Exchange on Friday amid vague takeover rumors swirling around the Canadian copper producer.
Rio Algom gained 3.30 to close at 35.80 in turnover of 589,000 shares on Canada's biggest stock market.
Analysts said the market rumors had Toronto-based Noranda Inc making an offer for Rio Algom. Noranda has operations in mining, forest products and oil and gas.
"That's what I've heard. To me it sounds like speculation," one mining analyst said.
Another mining analyst said the two companies would be a good fit. "Noranda has got a lot of cash and they (Rio Algom) have got a lot of good properties," the analyst said.
Rio Algom produces copper, molybdenum, uranium and coal from mines in Canada, the United States and Chile.
The company is developing a uranium property in the U.S. and participating in the construction of a major copper/gold mine in Argentina, both of which are scheduled to begin production in 1997.
It has begun a second expansion of its copper mine in Chile which will be completed in 1998. A major copper/zinc property in Peru and copper discovery in Chile are at the pre-feasibility stage.
Shares in Noranda closed up 0.30 at 29.15 on volume of 459,000 shares on the Toronto exchange.
